Theocracy is a form of government where power is held by the religious elite. Theocracies get to designate an heir from a list of candidates (except in a papacy government form). Although the choice does not affect the future heir's monarch skills (set at random), they give the player different effects and events once the heir comes into power.

Has access to the Divine idea group, unless changed by a government reform.

Type Effects Description & notes
Theocracy
  • +10% Clergy loyalty equilibrium
  • +5% Clergy influence
  • +10% Brahmins influence
 In a Theocarcy authority is derived from a divine power. The ruling class will often be the clergy itself and the head of state their leader.
  • Uses Devotion
  • Neither Rulers nor heirs can be generals
  • Has access to Divine ideas but not Aristocratic ideas

DevotionEdit

Please help with verifying or updating this section. It was last verified for version 1.23.

Devotion replaces legitimacy / republican tradition for theocracies and represents the zeal of the faith inside the country. Devotion increases from high stability and pious acts while decreasing from low stability and low religious unity.

When switching to a theocracy from another government form, the starting devotion value is set to the level of the nation's religious unity at the time.

EffectsEdit

The effects of devotion are proportional to its value (the table lists the major milestones):

Variable 0% 50% 100%
National tax modifier −25% 0 +25%
Yearly prestige −1 0 +1
Reform progress growth −25% 0 +25%
Clergy loyalty equilibrium −5% 0 +5%
Yearly papal influence −1 0 +1
Church power −25% 0 +25%
Monthly fervor −1 0 +1
Religious harmonization speed −25% 0 +25%
Yearly patriach authority −0.5 0 +0.5
Monthly piety accelerator −0.5 0 +0.5
Yearly doom reduction −0.25 0 +0.25
Yearly karma decay −0.05 0 +0.05

LeadershipEdit

Type Effects Description & notes
Clerical State
  • +10% National tax modifier
  • +10% Clergy loyalty equilibrium
This state is ruled by the clergy and uses the hierarchy of religious institutions for all government purposes.

Additional Effects:

  • Converting provinces grants +0.02 devotion
Monastic Order
  • −25% Fort maintenance
  • +0.25 Yearly army tradition
This country is ruled by the members of a Monastic Order. The order's hierarchy and rules replaces the need for most laws and administration.

Additional Effects:

  • Is a Monastic Order
  • Heirs and rulers can be generals
  • Religious unity affects devotion when changing religion
  • Fixed rank: Duchy
Millennialist Theocracy
  • +1 Monthly church power
  • +0.25 Monthly fervor
  • -25% Cost of enforcing religion through war
  • +10% Morale damage
  • −2 Yearly devotion
Based around the idea that the final judgement is coming and a period of Golden Age will occur on Earth prior to that, Millennialists are always looking for signs of the End.

Conditions :

Available only with the Domination DLC enabled.
  • Is not The Papal State
  • Religion is Protestant, Anglican, Reformed or Hussite

Additional effects :

  • When force converting a nation : Gain +1 devotion for every point of development that nation has
Patriarchate
  • +1 Clergy max privileges
  • +10% Clergy loyalty equilibrium
  • +1 Tolerance of the true faith
The authority of the Patriarch is the only one that can lead our country, as he is God's maximum representative.

Conditions :

  • Is not The Papal State
  • Religion is Orthodox
Feudal Theocracy
  • +1 Missionary
  • +1% Missionary strength
  • +2 Tolerance of the true faith
  • +50 Governing capacity
  • / +5% Clergy / Brahmins loyalty equilibrium
The State is ruled by a religious leader with the throne passing on within his divine sanctioned family.

Conditions:

  • Religion is in Muslim group
  • Unlocked by the following:
    • Starting with this government type ( Ardabil, Oman, Mzab, the Rassids and the Mushasha)
    • Forming Sokoto
    • Enacting the T6 reform "Hereditary Religious Leadership"

Additional effects:

  • Unlocks Divine ideas, while locking Aristocratic ideas.
Available only with the Cradle of Civilization DLC enabled.

Zoroastrian Theocracy
  • +2 Clergy max privileges
  • −20% Clergy influence
  • +15% Manpower in accepted culture provinces
A theocracy led by the ideals, ideas and traditions of the Zoroastrian faith. Led by the Mobeds, this theocracy discards ideas of tolerance in order to secure the future of Zoroastrianism.

Conditions :

  • Is not The Papal State
  • Religion is Zoroastrian

Additional effects :

Available only with the King of Kings DLC enabled.
  • Enables the "Three Royal Fires" mechanic:
    • The nation has acess to Asha Vahista, which scales from −100 to 100.
The nation gains the following modifier, scaling with its current Asha Vahishta:
Asha Vahishta −100 −50 0 50 100
Effects
  • +1 Monthly Asha Vahishta
  • +0.5 Monthly Asha Vahishta
 No effect
  • −1 National unrest
  • +12.5% Manpower in true faith provinces
  • +0.5 Monthly Three fires government power
  • −2 National unrest
  • +25% Manpower in true faith provinces
  • +1 Monthly Three fires government power
Asha Vahishta is increased/decreased by the following:
  • 0.2 monthly, always
  • 0.25 monthly, while at peace
  • +2: Creating an alliance
  • +5: Enforcing peace for a Zoroastrian nation
  • +0.5: Arranging a royal marriage
  • +1: Guaranteeing a country
  • +1: Sending gifts
  • +2: Taking on debts
  • +2: Influencing a nation
  • +50: Intervening in a war
  • −5: Breaking an alliance
  • −1 per development: Force religion in a peace deal (unless the Persian mission "The City of Daman" was completed)
  • −1 per development: Converting provinces (unless the Persian mission "Purify the Holy Sites" was completed)
  • −10: Threatening war
  • −5: Insulting
  • −1: Fabricating claim
  • −1: Breaking a royal marriage
Additionally every month, the government gathers 0.25 + 0.08 x the rulers respective skill in the three fires abilities.
While Asha Vahishta is at least −50, a three fires ability can be used once 100 progress in it has been gathered. Using one of the three fires reduces Asha Vahishta by −50 and resets that fires progress to 0.
Each modifier lasts for 10 years.

Meaning Heaven Dwelling, Ganden Phodrang is originally the name of the residential quarters of the Dalai Lama. As the Dalai Lama is both the spiritual and earthly leader of Tibet, Ganden Phodrang now refers too to all the system of government.

  • Culture is in Tibetan group
  • Religion is in Eastern group

Blessed Plutocracy
  • −25% Governing capacity modifier
  • +1 Merchant
  • +2 Yearly papal influence
  • +25% Curia treasury contribution
A theocracy where wealth and trade is playing a major role next to the Catholic church. The Holy See also allows us the selling of Indulgences to whoever needs them the most.

Conditions:

  • Has completed the Rigan missions "Compete with the Swedes", "Trade Presence in Lübeck" and "Papal Embassy"

Additional Effects:

  • Has merchant republic mechanics:
  • +25% State governing cost
  • −25% Trade company governing cost
    • Bonus goods production in provinces not owned by merchant republics or trade companies, proportional to percentage of trade power in the node (e.g., non-owned provinces produce 50% bonus goods if the republic controls 100% of trade in the node).
    • AI is more reluctant to be diplomatically vassalized by or as a merchant republic (−10 reasons if the proposer is and −30 reasons if the target is).
    Available only with the Wealth of Nations DLC enabled.
    • Vassals, marches, and client states, which usually do not transfer trade power to their overlord, will transfer 50% if the overlord is a merchant republic.
    • Has factions
    • Counts as a merchant republic[1]
    • Enables the Sell Indulgences diplomatic Option with Catholic nations
    • Enables the Plutocratic idea group, but disables the Divine idea group
Available only with the Res Publica DLC or the Mare Nostrum DLC enabled.
  • Can construct a trade post for 50 administrative power, giving +10 trade power, in one owned province per trade node (except the node containing the main trade city).
Available only with the Mare Nostrum DLC enabled.
  • Can lead a trade league and create trading cities.

Internal & External MissionEdit

Type Effects Description & notes
Internal Mission
  • +2 Tolerance of the true faith

External Mission

Our faith is at constant risk from heathens and heretics alike. The only ones who we can count on are other followers of our religion - our brothers and sisters in faith. It is our duty to protect them from the godforsaken forces of evil.

The seas are filled with heathens and villains plundering the trade and transport ships of the honest followers of our faith.   • +10% Trade efficiency
  • +10% Global trade power

  • +50% Promote culture cost
Centuries of fragmentation under the Holy Roman Empire have the Germans starkly disunited. This needs to be corrected.

Conditions:

Additional effects:

  • Effect when removing:
    • Remove all country modifiers: "Integrated Culture: X"
  • Cannot attain Cultural Union
  • Has access to the "Cultural Unity" mechanic:
    • The government has a "Cultural Unity" Bar which represents their progress in integrating a culture
    • The government can choose a culture to integrate via the "Choose culture to integrate" decision
    • Once the Bar reaches 100, the chosen culture will be "integrated", adding it as an accepted culture, without occupying a slot
    • "Cultural unity" is gained and lost as follows:
      • +0.83 monthly, always
      • +0.33 monthly, if the target culture is accepted
      • +0.001 monthly, per 1% of Religious unity
      • +0.1 monthly, while at peace
      • +0.5 monthly, after finishing Court ideas
      • −0.3 to +0.3 monthly, depending on Stability
      • −0.1 to +0.1 monthly, depending on Legitimacy (above or below 50)
      • −1 monthly, while not integrating a culture
      • −1 monthly, if our primary culture isn't in the Germanic group
      • −0.05 monthly, per point of War exhaustion
      • +1.5 when developing a province of that culture

  • −10% Idea cost
  • −10% Cost of advisors with ruler's culture

Type Effects Description & notes

  • +20% Average monarch lifespan

The priestly class serves the state by being a spiritual guidance of our people through difficult time periods. The clergy deserves an increase of their rights to honor their role in our state.

Conditions:

  • Is not a Pirate Republic
  • Is not revolutionary
  • Religion is either:
    • Animist
    • Totemist
    • Alcheringa
    • Inti
    • Nahuatl
    • Mayan
Embedded Norse Traditions
  • May raid coasts
  • +10% Clergy influence
  • +50% Army tradition from battles
  • +50% Naval tradition from battles
The religion of our ancestors is the driving force of our state's actions. Old, forgotten practices have returned and are now a central point of our society.

Conditions:

  • Is not a Pirate Republic
  • Is not revolutionary
  • Religion is Norse

Additional effects:

  • Winning wars increases Legitimacy (or its equivalents)
Fiqh Laws
  • +2% Missionary strength
  • +10% Clergy loyalty equilibrium
Fiqh is the knowledge of the Islamic rulings from their sources. As such, the Fiqh Laws are the result of codifying the laws of the Quran into our very own legal code.

Conditions:

Available only with the Domination DLC enabled.
  • Is not a Pirate Republic
  • Is not revolutionary
  • Religion is in Muslim group
  • At least one of:
    • Has completed the Ottoman mission "Codify the Fiqh" on the "Legalism" path of their branching missions
    • Has enacted the T1 government reform “Sultanate of Rûm”

Additional effects:

  • Vassals, Marches and Eyalets which follow our religion gain the following bonuses:
    • +25% Manpower in true faith provinces
    • +25% Global sailors modifier
    • +15% Production efficiency
  • Enables two decisions that move Piety by 200% towards the opposite side, if it currently is at least 50% towards either Mysticism or Legalism.
Sufism Decree
  • +1 Diplomat
  • +10% Dhimmi loyalty equilibrium
Sufism is a set of practices and a way of thinking focusing entirely on the spiritual and ritual nature of the Islam. Many of its traditions and influence have found their way into our own government.

Conditions:

Available only with the Domination DLC enabled.
  • Is not a Pirate Republic
  • Is not revolutionary
  • Religion is in Muslim group
  • At least one of:
    • Has completed the Ottoman mission "Codify Sufism" on the "Mysticism" path of their branching missions
    • Has enacted the T1 government reform “Sultanate of Rûm”

Additional effects:

Available only with the Golden Century DLC enabled.
  • The "Guaranteed Dhimmi Autonomy" Dhimmi estate privilege no longer increases Estate influence nor decreases Max absolutism
  • Unlocks the "Mevlevi" Holy order for Sunni and Ibadi nations
  • Unlocks the "Bektashi" Holy order for Shia and Ibadi nations
Most Holy Governing Synod
  • +5% Manpower in true faith provinces
  • +1 Missionary
  • +10% Clergy loyalty equilibrium
The power of the Patriarchy has been independent from the Emperor for far too long. By establishing the Most Holy Synod, the affairs of the church are now matters of the state and the Patriarchate is de facto abolished.

Conditions:

Available only with the Domination DLC enabled.
  • Is not a Pirate Republic
  • Is not revolutionary
  • At least one of:
    • Was unlocked via the Russian mission "The Most Holy Synod"
    • Has enacted the T1 government reform “Ruthenian Tsardom”
  • Religion is Orthodox

Additional effects:
While this reform is active, every owned province that has a Temple or a Cathedral:

  • Gain province modifier “Expanded Temple Rights”, giving the following effects:
    • −2 Local unrest
    • +33% Local tax modifier
  • Seizing land from the Clergy no longer triggers Rebels
Strengthened the Patriarchate
  • +1 Clergy max privileges
  • −15% Clergy influence
  • +20% Clergy loyalty equilibrium
  • +1 Tolerance of the true faith
  • +0.5% Yearly patriarch authority
State and Church are separate entities, each of them following their own agendas without intervening in the affairs of the other political body. The freedom of the Patriarchate is emphasized through several state reforms.

Conditions:

Available only with the Domination DLC enabled.
  • Is not a Pirate Republic
  • Is not revolutionary
  • At least one of:
    • Was unlocked via the Russian mission "The Most Holy Synod"
    • Has enacted the T1 government reform “Ruthenian Tsardom”
  • Religion is Orthodox

Additional effects:

  • The "Religious Culture" Clergy privilege no longer increases Clergy influence
Head of the Patriarchate
  • +10 Maximum absolutism
  • +20% Clergy loyalty equilibrium
  • +1 Tolerance of the true faith
  • +0.5% Yearly patriarch authority
State and Church are intertwined into one complete entity of the nation. The absolutist rule of the Emperor is supported by the Patriarchate.

Available only with the Domination DLC enabled.

  • Is not revolutionary
  • Was unlocked via the Russian mission "The Most Holy Synod"
  • Religion is Orthodox

While this reform is active, every owned province that has a Temple or a Cathedral:

Anglican State Church
  • +1 Tolerance of the true faith
  • +20% Church power

State and church are both in the hands of the monarch. Unlike many other Protestant branches, however, the government decides its religious matters with concepts taken from both Catholicism and the Reformation.

    • Religion is Hussite
Legacy of the Safavid
  • +10% Clergy loyalty equilibrium
  • +1.5% Missionary strength
  • +1 Clergy max privileges
  • −10% Clergy influence
The religious matters of the state are dominated by the Safaviyya and the members of the Safavid dynasty. While the clergy is still an important part of the state, many of its duties are relegated to the ruling family as they are the head of the order.

Military Doctrines and OrganizationEdit

Type Effects Description & notes
Organized Military Staff
  • −20% Reinforce cost
  • +25% Reinforce speed
  • +20% National supply limit modifier
By maintaining a vigorous organization of the military budget and keeping our military staff coordinated we can ensure that regiment losses can be recovered more easily.
Military Engineering
  • −25% Artillery barrage cost
  • −10% Artillery cost
A war is not only won through the discipline of our troops but also through the quality of our military equipment. Our doctrine should focus on the usage of superior artillery models which are cheaper to maintain.
Defensive Stance
  • +15% Fort defense
  • +20% Garrison size
  • +1 Max hostile attrition
Our greatest strength does not lie in our offensive capabilities but in our ability to hold our defenses. Letting enemies wear down on our walls will be our victory.

  • All of the following must be true:
    • Is not a March
    • Is not a Client State March
Reinforce the Sygnakhs
  • +15% Fort defense
  • +20% Garrison size
  • +1 Max hostile attrition
  • −25% Fort maintenance
  • +1 Attrition for enemies
  • −20% Recruitment time
The system of recruitment and defense across our nation, a set of fortifications used for rallying and defending our territories, has been standing guard between us and our foes for centuries. We must therefore take great care to maintain and improve it as time goes on.

  • −15% Land attrition

It is of great importance that our soldiers do not lose their discipline in the midst of battle. Only through our drill can we ensure the survival of our men.
Cavalry Warfare

Cavalry is the mobile force of our army and serves as shock troops in combat. Our military focuses on increasing its usage and on integrating them into our regiments.

Mercenary Leadership

Our state has put great emphasis on the usage of mercenaries. Where others use standing armies, we have a lasting contract with the many professional and well-equiped mercenaries.

Mansure Army
  • −50% Regiment drill loss
  • +50% Army drill gain modifier
  • +10% Infantry combat ability
  • −1% Yearly army tradition decay
The Mansure Army ("The Victorious Soldiers of Muhammad") is the great army of the Ottoman Empire after the dismantlement of the Janissary Corps. Unlike the corrupt Janissaries, the troops of the Mansure Army are based upon discipline, military knowledge from the Europeans, drill and loyalty to the Sultanate.

  • +20% Manpower recovery speed
The Green Standard Army is the imperial army of our state. Starting as deserted battalions, the army is now the primary military and police force of the state.

Available only with the Domination DLC enabled.
  • At least one of:
    • Culture is Jurchen
    • Culture is Manchu

Additional effects:

Ashigaru Regiments
  • +50% Army tradition from battles
  • −10% Infantry cost
The ubiquity of conflicts and wars in Japan during the Sengoku Jidai gave rise to a new class of warriors, the ashigaru. While peasants and technically not samurai, the easier accessibility to them in comparison to the samurai turned them into the backbone of any army. Armed with spears, bows and swords, their constant presence in battle made them into a class between the farmers and the samurai, being in some cases even considered as part of the lower strata of samurai. Hover, it was with the introduction of the tanegashima teppou, the Japanese adaption of the matchlock, that their presence truly shined. Its easier learning curve compared to the bow, combined with the superior numbers of the ashigaru compared to the samurai, made it so that ashigaru armed with matchlocks became the main part of any Japanese army.

Conditions:

Available only with the Domination DLC enabled.
  • Culture is in Japanese group
Early Bushido Code
  • +10% Samurai force limit
  • −1% Yearly army tradition decay
Bushido is a moral code dictating the attitude, behavior and lifestyle of the samurai. Though the code would get its mythical status in the centuries to come, its base concepts have been part of it ever since its first inception.

Conditions:

Available only with the Domination DLC enabled.
  • Culture is in Japanese group
Reform the Samurai
  • +50% Army drill gain modifier
  • +0.5 Yearly army tradition

While historically the Tercios were not only drafted from Spain, but also from Italy or Wallonia, the most valuable Tercios were drafted from Spanish provinces. Tercios were almost unbeatable for decades in the battlefields across Europe and the Mediterranean, and were key to the evolution of European warfare.

The guiding principle for how highly someone is ranked must be ability, and this route must be open regardless of religion or origin. Only this way can we be sure to raise a court of those most able to bring our empire forward.

Secularization?Edit

Type Effects Description & notes
Partial Secularisation
  • +1 Maximum tolerance of heretics
  • +1 Maximum tolerance of heathens
Though religion will always be at the heart of our administration, some sectors of our government must be secularized if we are to adapt to this changing world.
Strengthen Religious Head
  • +1 Yearly absolutism
  • +10 Maximum absolutism
We must strengthen the rule and abilities of our leader so that we can at all times be certain that the divine will is being carried out in accordance to their designs.
Hereditary Religious Leadership
  • Change to Monarchy with Feudal Theocracy reform
Many have come to regard our leaders not only as great spiritual and worldly leaders but as semi-divine beings themselves. Many followers have in fact formed a type of order together for the following of our ruler in all ways that is required. Let us reform our country so that all our subjects are in fact members of our sect.

Conditions:

  • is Muslim
Crowned Ruler
  • Changes government type to Monarchy
  • Lose 3 Stability
It is time we drop the trappings of religion and make our leader a monarch in own right.
Proclaim Republic
  • Changes government type to Republic
  • Lose 3 Stability
While we must never stray far from our religious roots it is also important that we allow our state to evolve. Let us create a free republic where the head of state is elected from among the group of valid candidates freely.
Magister Militum Dei
  • +1 Land leader fire
  • +10% Manpower in true faith provinces
Caedite eos. Novit enim Dominus qui sunt eius

Embrace Conciliarism

  • +50% Monthly favor growth modifier
Conciliarism insists that it is the Ecumenical Council, not the Pope, who holds supreme rulership over our country. By accepting this as truth in our faith and administration, we may vastly expand the power of the Cardinals and prevent the Papacy from falling under foreign influence.

  • Is The Papal State
Governing Senate
  • +10% All estates' loyalty equilibrium
  • −10% All estates' influence modifier

The governing senate is the assembly of our ruler's most trusted advisors and the highest legislative, judicial and executive institution of the empire. Unlike its predecessor, the boyar Duma, the senate covers the concerns of all the estates and senators.

Available only with the Domination DLC enabled.

Enforced Autocracy

Available only with the Domination DLC enabled.

Clergy in AdministrationEdit

Type Effects Description & notes

Religious conviction must be an integral part of our state in all its parts. When educating administrators among the clergy we must stress that they all get a sold grounding in theology so that they can take the right decisions at all times.

Divided Aristocracy

Economical MattersEdit

Type Effects Description & notes
Empower the Burghers
  • +5% Global trade power
  • +5% Trade efficiency
  • / +5% Burghers/ Vaishyas loyalty equilibrium

The Burghers are the traders and merchants of our state. They ensure that a constant stream of money finds its way into our state. To empower their privileges and their influence leads to a faster accumulation of our wealth.

  • Is not revolutionary
Curtail the Burghers
  • −10% Trade company governing cost
  • +15% Trade steering

The rights and privileges of the Burghers have been too vast for far too long. Wars and expansion of the state are confronted by a lack of support from our own class of merchants. It is time to curtail the rights of the traders and create a centralized state.

  • Is not revolutionary

Mercantilistic Approach
  • −10% Cost to promote mercantilism

Embrace Free Trade
  • +25% Institution spread

Embrace the Economic Theory
  • −0.5 Interest per Annum

Lockean Proviso
  • −5% Development cost

Our empire stretches far beyond our homeland and into far-flung colonies in our extended Outremer, our Lands Beyond The Sea. Additional effects:

  • Has access to parliament
Available only with the Domination DLC enabled.
  • Can establish trade protectorates
Modern Economics
  • +10% Trade efficiency
  • +10% Burghers loyalty equilibrium
Many countries promote a more traditional way of economics, depending on their lands instead of their merchants. By instead promoting a more mercantile character in our economy, our nation will be able to gain more trade goods from overseas.

Conditions:

  • Is Netherlands

Additional effects:

  • Strengthen the "Free Enterprise" Burghers privilege, with:
    • +10% Naval forcelimit modifier
    • −15% Light ship cost
Chinampa Farms
  • +5% Goods produced modifier
Chinampa farms, or Floating Gardens, allow us to further increase our agricultural output and allow our economy to focus on different sections, such as crafts and trade.

Conditions:

  • Has completed the Aztec mission "Chinampa Farms"

Additional effects:
While this reform is active, every owned province that produces Grain:

  • Gain province modifier “Chinampa Farm” , giving the following effects:
    • +25% Local goods produced modifier
    • −5% Local development cost

Divine CauseEdit

Type Effects Description & notes
Safeguard Holy Sites
  • +15% Fort Defense
  • / / +10% Clergy/ Brahmins/ Jains loyalty equilibrium
It is our holy duty to look after the holy pilgrimage sites under our control and to protect any pilgrims within our lands.
Combat Heresy
  • +10% Morale of armies
  • +5% Shock damage
In the mission to spread the true faith we must never waver in our conviction and be ready to root out heresy wherever it springs up.
Expulsion of Heathens
  • −5% Development cost
  • -15% Culture conversion cost
As our state grows so does our exposure to wrongful teachings. We must not tolerate heathens or heretics within our walls. Instead these people can come live in our cities only if they convert to the true faith.
Pursuit of Knowledge
  • −5% Technology cost
Our cause is not the defense of our religion nor the forceful expansion of the faith. Instead we focus on the very nature of being, the relationship of the mortal and the divine realms.

Additional Effects:

  • May see the Monarch Skills of the selectable Heirs
The Guru's Wisdom
  • +3% Missionary strength
  • +10% Institution spread
All across the Dharmic world, there are men and women alike who fully detach themselves from the material world and live isolated in the untamed countryside to attain enlightenment. To be a Sikh means to be a student, and by learning from these wise men and studying the works of the great Gurus of the Sikh religion, we may spread our enlightened vision across the world.

Conditions:

  • Religion is Sikh
Seven Provinces
  • +15% Manpower in same culture group provinces
  • +15% Manpower in primary culture provinces
The Dutch Seven Provinces, united in the Union of Utrecht in 1579, formed a collective powerhouse that laid the foundation for the modern Netherlands. Each province, including Holland, Zeeland, and Utrecht, retained distinct identities while collaborating for mutual defense and economic prosperity.

Conditions:

  • Is Netherlands

Additional effects:
While this reform is active:

  • Every owned province that is in the Low Countries region and whose Culture is in the same group as our country:
    • Gain province modifier “Seven Provinces Organization” , giving the following effects:
      • −10% Local development cost
      • +10% Local goods produced modifier
      • −25% Province governing cost
      • −10% Local construction cost
      • −10% Local construction time
  • Every owned province that is in the Europe Continent but that is not in the Low Countries region:
    • Gain province modifier “Seven Provinces Organization” , giving the following effects:
      • +25% Province governing cost
      • +33 Minimum local autonomy

Separation of PowersEdit

Type Effects Description & notes
Clerical Commission
  • −1 National unrest
  • +1 Diplomatic relations
  • -50% Envoy Travel time
We should divide the powers of the state between our religious leader and a commission of clerics. This commission will be charged with keeping the peace in our nation, and conducting diplomatic affairs on our leader’s behalf.

Additional Effects:

  • Unlocks the ability to change government rank
Divine Guidance
  • +15 Maximum absolutism
The people question if we should divide the power in our nation, but the power is already divided. The true leader of our state is divine in nature, and their will is interpreted by our leader here on Earth.
Constitutional Theocracy
  • −10 Years of separatism
The state exists for the sole purpose to serve the divine. But to be completely devoted to this purpose we must ensure that no weak-minded theocratic ruler can come to power to corrupt our cause.

Additional Effects:

  • Unlocks the ability to change government rank
Theocratic Democracy
  • −1 National unrest
We are divinest of all, but we must never forget the inherent divinity found in even the lowliest of commoners. By allowing our peasants to elect their own representatives, we allow them to have their own voice in the court of the divine.

Conditions:

  • Not available for Monastic Orders
  • Only available if the Nobility estate does not exist or if the Crown owns more lands than the Nobility estate and the Nobility loyalty is equal or higher than their influence.

Additional Effects:

  • Unlocks the ability to change government rank
  • Enables parliament
  • Disables the Nobility estate
  • Disables the "Call Diet" interaction
Regionally Elected Commanders
  • −1 National unrest
In our government, the successor to the current ruler is decided by a vote from the warriors who have dedicated their lives to protecting the Faith. By allowing the citizens of the towns and villages under our protection to partake in electing the Commander that represents their interests, we may begin to expand our administration and make those under our protection feel accurately represented in the Court of Commanders.

Conditions:

  • Only available for Monastic Orders
  • Only available if the Nobility estate does not exist or if the Crown owns more lands than the Nobility estate and the Nobility loyalty is equal or higher than their influence

Additional Effects:

  • Unlocks the ability to change government rank
  • Enables parliament
  • Disables the nobility estate
  • Disables the "Call Diet" interaction
Open Public Elections
  • −15% Stability cost modifier
Many villages under our protection demand representation, and although they are fools who do not understand that the Commander’s rulership is divine, we must grant them some concessions if we are to keep them happy. Traditionally, only Commanders would vote for the new leader of our Order, but by opening elections to the public and establishing two new subdivisions of our Order for the people to vote for, they may feel their interests are represented by the state.

Additional Effects:

  • Unlocks the ability to change government rank
  • Can not be elected the Emperor of the HRE
Available only with the Res Publica DLC enabled.
  • Elections held every 4 years and when the ruler dies
  • Does not have Heirs
  • Enables the "Militarists vs. Theocrats" mechanic:
    • Choice between a Militarist and a Theocrat candidate with random stats and no re-election possible, each side gathering power from the player's choices. Its possible to see their stats before choosing
Militarists in power: Theocrats in power:
+20% Manpower recovery speed +2% Missionary strength
+50% Army tradition from battles +2 Tolerance of the true faith
−15% War score cost vs other religions +0.5 Yearly devotion

While the scale is at 0, the Militarists will be in power.

A Dynastic Theocracy
  • +1 Land leader fire
  • −20% Harsh treatment cost
  • +0.25 Yearly devotion
Faith will always play a vital role in our state, but it is becoming clear that our government is not adaptable enough to rule vast swathes of land and function in this changing world. There is no reason that our men of faith must swear themselves into celibacy and by reorganizing our state into a Dynastic Theocracy and granting our rulers royal titles, we will become protectors of the faith and the crown, guided by our Theocratic King.

Additional Effects:

  • Unlocks the ability to change government rank
  • Does not have heirs
  • Has consorts
  • Allows royal marriage
  • A general becomes ruler when the current ruler dies
Lords of the Sea
  • +0.25 Yearly devotion
  • +1 Naval leader fire
  • +15% Naval morale
The good work our soldiers have done in securing safe passage for pilgrims across the sea has made our sails a feared sight for pirates and heathens alike. However, it has become clear that the threat pirates pose to our faith go far beyond our small shores, and we must expand our order to become an Empire in itself if we are to properly serve our holy mission. By enacting a series of reforms within our government, we shall vastly expand our administration beyond our borders and our valiant Knights will elect all future commanders based on the number of pirate lords they have brought to kneel before God!

Conditions:

  • Capital has a port

Additional Effects:

  • Unlocks the ability to change government rank
  • Does not have an heir
  • Has consorts
  • Allows royal marriages
  • An admiral becomes ruler when the current ruler dies

The Nature of Our FaithEdit

Type Effects Description & notes
Faith and Power
  • −10% Morale damage received
Combat and power are the only ways to come closer to divine. Through victories on the battlefield, the people of our state show their piety and devotion.

Additional Effects:

  • Winning battles which are lead by the Ruler increases Devotion by 0.5 and Absolutism by 0.1
  • Rulers can be generals
Belief and Unity
  • +50% Religious unity
  • +2 Max promoted cultures
Faith is the unifying power which keeps the state and the people together. The government exists for the mere purpose to ensure that this unity remains unbroken.
Church and State
  • +1 Free policies
The faith and the state are the two pillars that hold up the world. Our laws are holy laws and they cannot be questioned.

Conditions:

  • Religion is not in Pagan religion group
God and Man
  • +1 Missionaries
  • +2 Tolerance of the true faith
The only relationship that matters is that between lowly mortals and the immortal holy spirits. Our state exists merely to remind people of the proper ways to devote themselves to prayer.

Conditions:

  • Religion is not in Pagan religion group
Organize Our Faith
  • +1 Yearly devotion
  • +1 Yearly absolutism
We are a highly organized state oriented around a faith that is itself highly disorganized. By attempting to enact an official hierarchy for our religion, we may begin to convert more followers to the true ways of the Gods.

Conditions:

  • Religion is in Pagan religion group
Soul and Body
  • +1 Tolerance of heretics
  • +1 Tolerance of heathens
  • +20% Religious harmonization speed
We must never forget that the barriers of culture and language are merely an illusion. We are all mere souls inhabiting a shell. It does not matter what language we speak, only that we service the divine in the proper way.

Conditions:

  • is Confucian

Culture, Faith and StateEdit

Type Effects Description & notes
Religious Society
  • +250 Governing capacity
Religion and culture are intertwined. No man of our society can claim to be of our culture if they do not follow the same rituals.
Harmonization of Cultures
  • −50% Promote culture cost
  • −20% Cost of advisors with ruler's culture
The concept of culture is in many ways similar to religion, though it is forged by traditions, social values and environment and not by divine enlightenment. The cultures within our state are bound to harmonize with each other as long they are following the true faith.
Cultural Safe Haven
  • +10% Manpower in accepted culture provinces
  • +10% Manpower in same culture group provinces
Cultures are fabricated social norms, created by men to differentiate them from others. In actuality, we are all mortal bodies walking on this world. Only the conviction to the true divine being is of importance.
Taxation of Foreigners
  • +50% National tax modifier
The culture of minorities is of little concern to us. As long they are willing to sacrifice part of their income for the holy cause, they are free to live out their traditions.

Additional Effects:

Available only with the Cradle of Civilization DLC enabled.
  • 25% chance to not lose Base Tax when exploiting provinces of the own Culture group
  • 50% chance to not lose Base Tax when exploiting provinces of foreign Culture group

Our Faith and the WorldEdit

Type Effects Description & notes
Priestly Autonomy
  • +2.5% Administrative efficiency
  • -5% Minimum autonomy in territories
No priest should hold power over another priest, with the exception of our ruler. Each realm shall be fully autonomous, and priests will remain free to interpret the will of the Gods in any way that is true to them.
State of Theologians
  • +2 Possible advisors
  • −20% Advisor cost
Our religion is no weapon or justification of war. Nor does it exist for monetary sake. Our faith is the result of intellectual and spiritual theories, discussions and understanding. The theology is the purpose of the state and its subjects.
Divinity through Craftsmanship
  • −2.5% Development cost modifier
  • +10% Goods produced modifier
The theologians discuss the means of reaching divine enlightenment, but only few realize what truly brings us closer to the immortal realm. The act of creation is the only holy way to approach our maker.
One State Under God
  • −30% War score cost vs other religions
Our faith and our state have become totally synonymous with each other. We are our religion, and any who devote themselves to the divine, must also devote themselves to the state.

Conditions:

  • Religion is not in Pagan religion group
The Global Crusade
  • −50% Cost of enforcing religion through war
This world is full of heretics, heathens, sinners, and blasphemers! We must seek to correct heretics and heathens alike, and spread our peaceful ways through force!

Conditions:

  • Religion is not Confucian or in Pagan religion group

Additional Effects:

  • Has access to the "Great Holy War" CB :
    • The "Great Holy War" CB allows you to target neighboring Heathens and Heretics, similar to the "Deus Vult" CB
      • If the T2 government reform "Mission to Civilize" is enacted, you may also target neighboring Pagans
      • If the "Deus Vult" CB is unlocked, you may also target non neighboring nations
  • All countries which get force converted by a country with this reform gain the country modifier “Global Crusader State” for 10 years, giving the following effects:
    • +1 Missionary
    • +3% Missionary strength
    • +50% Religious unity
    • −100% Missionary maintenance
The Many Fingers of God
  • +2 Tolerance of heretics
  • +2 Tolerance of heathens
We believe that there is only one God, by whom we live and by whom we die, and for whom we have an upright heart. But as God gives us the different fingers of the hand, so he gives to men diverse ways to approach him.

Conditions:

  • The Humanist idea group is completed
Proclaim Religious Head
  • −25% War score cost vs other religions
  • +1 Diplomatic reputation
We have organized our faith and now we are ready to emulate the heathens across our borders by proclaiming the leader of our state to also hold supreme leadership over our entire faith!

Conditions:

  • Religion is in Pagan religion group and no other country with the same religion has passed this reform
  • Is not subject to a country with the same religion
All Under Tengri
  • +15% Cavalry combat ability
  • +25% Cavalry to infantry ratio
All that is under the sky is under Tengri, and all that is under Tengri belongs to us. With the great eagle soaring high in the heavens, we will not rest until the entire world is brought to kneel before Tengri!

Conditions:

  • Religion is Tengri
Table of Ranks
  • +2.5% Administrative efficiency
  • +1 Free policies
The Empire needs a strong rulership free from the ambitions and intrigues of the boyars. The Table of Ranks restructures the hierarchical system of the Nobility, rewarding merit in the matters of military, bureaucracy and other subjects of the government. The nobles are bound to the Emperor by their personal service.

Conditions:

Available only with the Domination DLC enabled.
  • Is not a Pirate Republic
  • Has completed the Russian mission "The Table of Ranks"

Additional effects:

  • Enables the "Table of Ranks" interactions:
Icon Ability Cost Effects
Appoint Chancellor 45 An advisor of your choice will join the court. This advisor will be 50% cheaper to employ.
Appoint General Admiral 10 Gain an admiral with 100 Tradition. This admiral will additionally gain +1 Fire and +2 Maneuver pips.
Appoint General Field Marshal 10 Gain an general with 100 Tradition. This general will additionally gain +1 Siege and +2 Fire pips.
